text: A call to your own database costs fractions of a cent and single-digit milliseconds. A call to an LLM provider costs real, metered money and can take seconds. That gap is why caching matters more for AI apps than for a typical API.
A cache hit isn't just faster -- it's a call you simply don't pay for. That dollar case is specific to AI, where each uncached call has a real, metered cost.

Exact-match caching returns a stored response for an identical prompt -- simple, but narrow, since real users rarely phrase the same question the same way twice. Semantic caching compares embeddings, so two differently-worded questions can still hit the same cached answer. A retrieval cache, for RAG apps, caches the retrieved context separately from the final answer.

Static knowledge and documentation lookups are safe to cache aggressively. Live data, personalized responses, and anything where stale is worse than slow need a real invalidation plan -- a stale semantic-cache hit reads as fluent and on-topic, and is simply wrong.
Caching cuts cost and latency, but only with deliberate rules about what's safe to reuse. Next up: what to do with the requests a cache can't absorb -- queueing and async processing.
